cohort: The study participants were infants enrolled in the MAGIC (Microbiome, Antibiotics and Growth Infant Cohort) study, from whom longitudinal fecal samples and associated clinical metadata were obtained.
finding: Fungal richness increased and mycobiome composition changed in a similar ordered pattern during the first 2 years of life, with antibiotic exposure and breastfeeding status contributing to time-specific mycobiome compositional variation.
mod_finding: Candida albicans exhibited altered abundance dynamics in association with birth mode, though post hoc analyses suggested this association might be driven by perinatal antibiotic exposure in children delivered by cesarean section.
